PullRequest.Title: [1.138] Show effective sandbox policy in Copilot agent sessions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

fixes #330986

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/488e7175-f206-4c6a-b49e-4b1d6bab2552

Backport #335918 to `release/1.138` by cherry-picking commit `adc9092582503ef136344e5d017aa68b3c10c944` with provenance (`git cherry-pick -x`).

Backport commit: `fe1417b0daa`. The cherry-pick applied without conflicts or release-specific code changes. The original PR against `main` remains unchanged.

## Changes

- Add `/sandbox-policy` completion for Copilot agent-host sessions, mapping it to the SDK's existing `/sandbox policy` command without starting a model turn or changing sandbox enforcement.
- Persist a uniquely named Markdown report for each invocation and show an **Open Sandbox Policy** preview link in chat.
- Keep SDK mapping, argument validation, ANSI cleanup, report formatting, and persistence in the sandbox display implementation. Propagate SDK and file-write failures instead of emitting broken links.
- Introduce optional command invocation/output hooks with fallbacks to existing SDK behavior; support structured text and link output with optional Markdown/preview flags.
- Preserve preview metadata across local and remote Agent Host URI rewriting, use theme-aware chat link colors, and support mouse and keyboard activation.
- Reuse a single-anchor rendering helper to avoid a second anchor scan and duplicate widget registration. Reuse shared SDK command metadata types.
- Add accessible-help guidance, unit coverage, and dark/light visual fixtures.

## Compatibility

Existing commands retain their default invocation, rendering, and lifecycle when no custom handler applies. No SDK dependency updates, additional permissions, or sandbox enforcement changes are included.

## Release-branch validation

- **801 targeted tests passed** across Copilot sessions, command handlers, completion, inline anchors, Markdown content, URI rewriting, and accessibility help.
- Core typecheck and transpile watchers completed with zero errors after the cherry-pick.
- `git diff origin/release/1.138...HEAD --check` passed.
- Branch contains only the requested cherry-picked commit on top of `release/1.138`.

The original change additionally passed ESLint, CSS lint, and dark/light visual checks. Coverage includes a 1,001-link response with one anchor scan, optional-hook fallbacks, report snapshots and failures, local/remote links, and keyboard activation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke `/sandbox-policy` or the existing `/sandbox policy` command and display its report
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The turn applies mode, awaits one SDK `commands.invoke`, formats the returned policy, awaits one session-data file write, then emits the Markdown link and completes. The write is newly on the response critical path; rendering's later file stat is not awaited by the turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the SDK sandbox command with `policy` input
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one invocation per accepted policy command
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing `/sandbox policy` route already invoked the same SDK command once; the new `/sandbox-policy` alias maps to that existing invocation without adding fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before any policy response can be emitted

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the formatted policy to a uniquely named Markdown file in per-session data
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one write and one retained file per successful policy invocation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The SDK text/message was emitted directly and no report file was written.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the response link is emitted

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Formatting and bytes written scale linearly with the SDK policy text; retained files scale with explicit policy-command invocations during the lifetime of a persisted session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serialized command invocation and one serialized write per user invocation; turns are processed through the session turn lifecycle rather than fanned out over policy entries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The synthetic `/sandbox-policy` command resolves without command-catalog discovery. Native `/sandbox policy` uses the provider's cached/coalesced command catalog. Report files deliberately use unique UUID paths and are not reused; the enclosing session-data directory is deleted when the session is removed and orphan directories are garbage-collected at startup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the awaited RPC, linear formatting, unique path, awaited write, and session-data cleanup ownership are explicit in the changed code and service implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Policy reports and manual invocation counts are not bounded in code, but realistic reports are small and invocation frequency is user-driven; session deletion bounds lifetime. This does not establish material latency or storage growth warranting a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The single write and snapshot retention are intrinsic to the requested persistent preview, have no per-rule boundary fan-out, and are cleaned with session data.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request slash-command completions while typing in a Copilot agent-host session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each eligible completion request concurrently obtains runtime commands and session customizations, then filters/sorts candidates before returning UI suggestions. A cold command catalog can wait up to 300 ms; warm requests use the cached catalog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced call on a cold/invalidated catalog, not one call per command; zero SDK calls on warm cache hits
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached command-list lookup and timeout were used before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold completion waits up to the existing timeout; warm completion is local

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Local filtering scales with runtime command count on each slash-typing event; the downstream completion provider already iterates and sorts that same small command catalog.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runtime-command and customization lookups run in `Promise.all`; command catalog refreshes are coalesced through one `inFlight` promise, and command-change events invalidate the cache.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold catalog lookup is cached and concurrent misses coalesce. The diff allocates a filtered array and prepends one synthetic command on each completion request, but does not defeat the SDK catalog cache or increase boundary-call count.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added linear copy and unchanged coalesced IPC behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime command catalogs are expected to contain tens rather than large collections; no evidence shows the extra filter/copy materially affects typing latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Boundary cardinality and cold/warm behavior are unchanged, and the added local pass is dominated by existing candidate construction and sorting.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render chat Markdown containing the new preview link, including local and remote Agent Host sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Markdown rendering rewrites internal link targets, scans anchors once, and synchronously parses query-bearing anchors to identify preview metadata. A matching preview anchor constructs one inline widget. Its file `stat` is asynchronous and fire-and-forget, so it is off the initial render's awaited critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve `stat` for the preview resource through the file service, potentially via the Agent Host filesystem provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous stat per newly rendered preview widget; normally one for each policy-command response
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary response links were not converted to inline file widgets here, so the policy preview link and its stat did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited for initial display; only a directory result can later update icon classes

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Synchronous query parsing scales with query-bearing anchors in a rendered response; filesystem stats scale only with anchors explicitly tagged `vscodeLinkType=markdown-preview`, whose normal effective cardinality is one per policy invocation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One DOM scan per rendered Markdown part. Preview widgets independently issue their file stats with no limiter, so effective stat concurrency equals the number of preview links in that rendered part; the intended policy response contributes one.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No stat cache is added, but unchanged Markdown parts are reused when content is identical. Streaming rerenders rebuild the part when content changes; the policy command emits its complete link in a single terminal response rather than token streaming. URI rewriting preserves preview metadata without network access.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the single-scan path, metadata filter, widget construction, and asynchronous stat call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Arbitrary model-authored content could manufacture many tagged links, but no realistic product path in the diff does so; the supplied feature creates one link.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The implementation avoids a second anchor scan, unchanged responses are reusable, and the only new boundary is one off-critical-path stat for the intended one-link response.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate Open Sandbox Policy and load the Markdown preview
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A mouse or keyboard gesture invokes the opener once with the Markdown preview editor override; opening then reads the persisted report through the local or Agent Host file provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open/read the persisted policy file in the Markdown preview editor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open operation per explicit click or key activation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No persisted policy preview link existed; existing links used their normal associated editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to display the requested preview after the user gesture

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales only with explicit activations and report byte size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One opener call per user activation; no loop, burst, or speculative preload is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Editor/model caching is delegated to the existing opener and Markdown preview subsystem; the diff neither bypasses nor duplicates that caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new metadata selects the existing preview editor and makes exactly one opener call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem/provider latency varies between local and remote sessions, but no extra open or read is added beyond the requested preview.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because the boundary is user-requested, singular, and necessary for the feature.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 19 changed files. Traced command discovery/invocation, policy formatting and persistence, session-data cleanup, URI rewriting, Markdown rendering, widget filesystem stats, and preview opening. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found; no findings were submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
